issues.title: Context + Tool Credibility POC
issues.body:
**Definition of Done**

## Ollama server + client updates

### Server

- [ ] In `desktop/src-tauri/src/ollama/server.rs`, we should define a `const` at the top of the file which is a "list" of `REQUIRED_OLLAMA_MODELS`, which for now will be:
  - [`llama-guard3:1b`](https://ollama.com/library/llama-guard3)
  - [`qwen3:1.7b`](https://ollama.com/library/[llama-guard3](qwen3:1.7b))
- [ ] Also in `desktop/src-tauri/src/ollama/server.rs`, in `Service`, we should define a `ensure_required_models_are_downloaded`. This should ensure that all of the models specified in `REQUIRED_OLLAMA_MODELS` are downloaded and, if not, download any missing ones in parallel (for the downloading we should add a `download_model` function to `OllamaClient` in `desktop/src-tauri/src/ollama/client.rs`, which this function calls). It should use the `OllamaClient.model_is_available` function to determine which models are available.
- [ ] In the `setup` portion of `run` in `desktop/src-tauri/src/lib.rs`, we should call `ensure_required_models_are_downloaded`

### Client

- [ ] `OllamaClient` in `desktop/src-tauri/src/ollama/client.rs` should define a `model_is_available` method which takes a model name (string) and returns a boolean
- [ ] `OllamaClient` in `desktop/src-tauri/src/ollama/client.rs`, should define new `guard_llm_prompt_evaluation`, and `guard_llm_tool_evaluation` functions (see [here](https://learnprompting.org/docs/prompt_hacking/defensive_measures/llm_eval) for a description of how this should work). These should use the [`llama-guard3:1b` model](https://ollama.com/library/llama-guard3) (which downloading of the model will be handled by the Ollama server, see above). There is a great system prompt that you should use here mentioned on [this page](https://learnprompting.org/docs/prompt_hacking/defensive_measures/llm_eval). The model should also be prompted to return ONLY text in the form of `{"credible": <boolean>, "reason": <string>}`. That text should then be deserialized to a struct and returned from this function. At the top of this function, use `model_is_available`, if false, just return "None" (callers of this function should act accordingly). `guard_llm_prompt_evaluation`, and `guard_llm_tool_evaluation` should be very small functions, which basically just define a system prompt and call `guard_llm_evaluation` with the appropriate system prompt.
- [ ] Update `OllamaClient.generate_title` to _always_ use the `qwen3:1.7b` model (the function doesn't need to take a `model` argument, and callers of this function should be updated as such). At the top of `generate_title` function, use `model_is_available`, if false, just return "None" (existing callers of this function should be updated accordingly)

## Prompt + Tool Credibility

- [ ] Create a new directory, `desktop/src-tauri/src/credibility` which looks like this:
  - `desktop/src-tauri/src/credibility/mod.rs` - just imports the `PromptCredibilityService` and `ToolCredibilityService` for now
  - `desktop/src-tauri/src/credibility/prompt.rs` - defines a `Service` which has a single function, `evaluate_prompt_credibility`, which implements a "Separate LLM Evaluation" POC (see [here](https://learnprompting.org/docs/prompt_hacking/defensive_measures/llm_eval) for a description of how this should work). For now this function should just call `OllamaClient.guard_llm_prompt_evaluation`.
  - `desktop/src-tauri/src/credibility/tool.rs` - defines a `Service` which has a single function, `evaluate_tool_call_credibility`, which implements a "Separate LLM Evaluation" POC (see [here](https://learnprompting.org/docs/prompt_hacking/defensive_measures/llm_eval) for a description of how this should work). For now this function should just call `OllamaClient.guard_llm_tool_evaluation`.

### Update LLM provider proxy

#### Backend

- [ ] `proxy_chat_request` in `desktop/src-tauri/src/gateway/llm_providers/ollama.rs` should make a "blocking call" to `PromptCredibilityService.evaluate_prompt_credibility`, which should basically pass in the `ChatMessage`, and this eventually gets passed down to `OllamaClient.guard_llm_prompt_evaluation`, and dynamically set in the system prompt that you define there (see above). If `credible` returned from `PromptCredibilityService.evaluate_prompt_credibility` is False, this should "short-circuit" the request to the LLM provider and instead return a "new" message to the client
- [ ] `call` in `desktop/src-tauri/src/gateway/mcp_proxy.rs` should make a "blocking call" to `ToolCredibilityService.evaluate_tool_call_credibility`, which should basically pass in the `ChatMessage`, and this eventually gets passed down to `OllamaClient.guard_llm_tool_evaluation`, and dynamically set in the system prompt that you define there (see above). If `credible` returned from `ToolCredibilityService.evaluate_tool_call_credibility` is False, this should "short-circuit" the request to the LLM provider and instead return a "new" message to the client

#### Frontend

- [ ] If `/llm/:provider/api/chat` determines that the LLM prompt is not credible, it should act accordingly and show the user a warning message as the last message in `ChatHistory`

linked_prs.title: feat: add MCP tool analysis feature
linked_prs.body:
## Overview

This PR implements automatic tool analysis for MCP (Model Context Protocol) servers using Ollama's phi3:3.8b model. The feature analyzes each tool to determine its characteristics: whether it reads data, writes data, is idempotent, and is reversible.

## Key Features

### 🔍 Automatic Tool Analysis
- Analyzes MCP tools using local Ollama model (phi3:3.8b)
- Determines four key properties for each tool:
  - **is_read**: Whether the tool primarily reads/retrieves data
  - **is_write**: Whether the tool creates, updates, or deletes data
  - **idempotent**: Whether the tool can be safely called multiple times
  - **reversible**: Whether the tool's effects can be undone

### 💾 Database Integration
- New `tools` table to persist tool metadata and analysis results
- Foreign key relationship to `mcp_servers` with cascade delete
- Stores tool schemas and analysis timestamps

### 🔄 Background Processing
- Non-blocking analysis - tools are saved immediately
- Analysis happens asynchronously in the background
- Batch processing (10 tools at a time) for performance
- Graceful fallback if Ollama model isn't available

### 🎨 Enhanced UI
- Tool properties displayed in `ToolHoverCard` component
- Color-coded indicators (green for safe, orange for caution)
- Real-time status updates (awaiting model, in progress, completed)
- Analysis results help users understand tool capabilities and risks

## Technical Details

### Architecture
- **Tool ID Format**: `{mcp_server_id}__{tool_name}` (double underscore separator)
- **Periodic Updates**: UI polls for analysis updates every 5 seconds
- **Model Management**: Waits for phi3:3.8b model to be available before analysis

### API Endpoints
- `GET /api/mcp_server/tools` - Returns all available tools with analysis results

### Database Schema
```sql
CREATE TABLE tools (
  id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
  mcp_server_id TEXT NOT NULL,
  name TEXT NOT NULL,
  description TEXT,
  input_schema TEXT,
  is_read INTEGER,
  is_write INTEGER,
  idempotent INTEGER,
  reversible INTEGER,
  analyzed_at TEXT,
  created_at TEXT,
  updated_at TEXT
)
```

## Changes Summary

- Added new database table and migrations for tools
- Implemented `ToolModel` for database operations
- Enhanced `OllamaClient` with `analyzeTools()` method
- Modified `SandboxedMcpServer` to trigger analysis on tool discovery
- Updated UI components to display analysis results
- Added OpenAPI schema definitions for new types

## Breaking Changes

None - this feature is fully backward compatible.

## Testing

The feature includes graceful error handling:
- Tools are saved even if analysis fails
- Analysis can be retried for unanalyzed tools
- UI shows appropriate status messages during analysis

## Future Improvements

- Re-analysis capability for tools when their schemas change
- Configurable analysis model (currently hardcoded to phi3:3.8b)
- Manual override for analysis results
- Export analysis results for auditing

2.3.1

  • #7789 d5b416e Thanks @​fronterior! - Fixed the LSP method workspace/didChangeWorkspaceFolders to perform incremental updates instead of replacing the entire folder list.

Updates `@opentelemetry/exporter-trace-otlp-http` from 0.54.2 to 0.207.0
Release notes

Sourced from @​opentelemetry/exporter-trace-otlp-http's releases.

experimental/v0.207.0

0.207.0

:boom: Breaking Changes

  • feat(sdk-node)!: drop lazy-loading of jaeger exporter #5989 @​pichlermarc
    • (user-facing): setting OTEL_TRACE_EXPORTER=jaeger not instantiate a Jaeger exporter anymore, please use OTEL_TRACE_EXPORTER=otlp instead.
      • Jaeger now has native API support for OTLP and Jaeger's Thrift API endpoints have been deprecated
  • feat(otlp-exporter-base): check OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_CERTIFICATE and other related env vars when resolving configuration for OTLP HTTP exporters #6015 @​david-luna

:rocket: Features

  • feat(sdk-node): always set up propagtion and context manager #5930
    • using (new NodeSDK).start() will now automatically set up a context management and propagation, even if no Trace SDK is initialized.
  • feat(otlp-exporter-base, otlp-grpc-exporter-base): add an option to let an SDK distribution prepend their own user-agent string in HTTP & GRPC exporters #5928 @​david-luna
  • feat(web): add session handling implementation 5173 @​martinkuba

:bug: Bug Fixes

  • fix(sdk-logs): Fix the batchLogProcessor exporting only upon _scheduledDelayMillis and ignoring maxExportBatchSize #5961 @​jacksonweber

linked_prs.title: fix: infinite tool analysis loading in UI sidebar
linked_prs.body:
This PR fixes an issue where the UI sidebar would show infinite loading states for tool analysis.

## Problem

The tool analysis loading spinner in the UI sidebar would continue indefinitely for certain MCP servers, particularly the filesystem server. This was due to incorrect cache key lookups when matching tools with their analysis results.

## Root Cause

The filesystem MCP server's tools have IDs formatted like:
`modelcontextprotocol__servers__src__filesystem__servers__src__filesystem__read_file`

However, the cached tool analysis was stored with just the tool name (e.g., `read_file`). The original logic would extract `servers__src__filesystem__read_file` as the tool name, which didn't match the cache key of `read_file`.

## Solution

Updated the cache key extraction logic to find the last occurrence of `__` and extract everything after it. This ensures that for complex tool IDs, we correctly extract just the actual tool name for cache lookup.

## Testing

Added comprehensive unit tests in `sandboxedMcp.test.ts` to verify:
- Standard tool naming (simple prefix)
- Filesystem server tools with complex prefixes
- Proper matching of tools with cached analysis results
- Correct status display (completed vs awaiting_ollama_model)

## Other Changes

- Cleaned up redundant dynamic imports of stores
- Minor refactoring in OAuth flow handlers
- Removed unnecessary complexity in various modules

Closes #404

Fixes #490

## Summary

Fixed the MemoriesMessage component to properly handle memory values that contain newline characters.

- Updated parsing logic to properly identify memory keys vs multi-line values
- Memory keys are now detected by looking for lines with colons that look like key names
- Multi-line values are preserved and displayed correctly using whitespace-pre-wrap
- Fixed issue where file_content memory with newlines was displayed as separate memory items

issues.title: Selecting a non-ollama model (ex. an OpenAI model) does not persist it in localStorage
issues.body: It seems that the logic in `desktop_app/src/ui/stores/ollama-store/index.ts` will properly get/set an _ollama_ model to local storage, such that when you reload/reopen the app, that ollama model is preselected in the dropdown. We may want to extract "selectedModel" from the "ollama store" (move it to chat store?) since we support not just ollama models anymore: **Definition of Done** - If I select an ollama model and reopen the app, that model is preselected (if it is still present) - If I select a non-ollama model (ex. `gpt-4o` from OpenAI) and reopen the app, that model is preselected (if it is still present)

linked_prs.title: fix: Move `selectedModel` from `ollama-store` to `chat-store` for proper persistence
linked_prs.body:
Fixes #492

## Description
This PR moves the `selectedModel` state from the ollama store to the chat store to ensure that both ollama and non-ollama models (like OpenAI models) persist their selection across app restarts.

## Changes
- Moved `selectedModel` state and `setSelectedModel` action from ollama-store to chat-store
- Added localStorage persistence to chat-store using Zustand's persist middleware
- Updated all components to use `selectedModel` from chat-store instead of ollama-store
- Removed persist middleware from ollama-store as it's no longer needed

ai_judgment.response: Yes. This issue involves LLM provider usage, specifically the persistence of selected LLM models (e.g., OpenAI's GPT-4). It relates to memory mechanisms and model selection logic, which are unique to agent systems.

issues.body: # OpenWebUI Streaming Support for Chat Completions ## Description The OpenWebUI integration currently fails when using streaming responses. While non-streaming requests work correctly, streaming chat completions return a 500 error. ## Current Status - [x] `/models` endpoint - Fixed - [x] `/api/proxy/openai/chat/completions` (non-streaming) - Fixed - [ ] `/api/proxy/openai/chat/completions` (streaming) - **Needs fixing** ## How to Connect OpenWebUI 1. First you need to start the platform by following https://www.archestra.ai/docs/platfrom-developer-quickstart 2. Launch OpenWebUI, where platform is address is `OPENAI_API_BASE_URL=http://host.docker.internal:9000/api/proxy/openai`: ```bash docker run --rm -p 3001:8080 \ -e ENABLE_OPENAI_API=true \ -e OPENAI_API_BASE_URL=http://host.docker.internal:9000/api/proxy/openai \ -e OPENAI_API_KEY=sk-proj-... \ -v open-webui:/app/backend/data \ --name open-webui \ ghcr.io/open-webui/open-webui:main ``` 3.
